seo.title: How to Take a Passport or Visa Photo at Home | FlyFrame
seo.description: Take a clean passport or visa photo at home with your phone: distance, straight pose, daylight, plain background, no glasses. Then bring it to the editor.

hero.title: How to take a Passport & Visa Photo at Home
hero.intro: Start with a well-taken photo at home, and let our editor do the rest. Follow this guide to capture a photo that's ready for editing and meets your country's requirements.

image.alt: A phone showing the guide, with a woman taking a photo of herself and a cross-to-tick bar below

items.label: Camera
items.text: A phone with a camera, ideally the rear camera, on a stand or tripod if you have one.

items.label: Wall
items.text: Try to choose a plain wall with no decorations or objects in the background.

items.label: Light
items.text: Position yourself facing the window for soft, natural, even lighting.

items.label: Helper
items.text: A helper, a timer, or something steady to prop the phone on.

items.title: Camera setup
items.alt: Person standing in front of a phone on a tripod, 40 to 50 cm away

points: Use your phone's [rear camera](/guide/rear-vs-front-camera) whenever possible.
Keep the camera at **eye level** and **level with the ground**.
Place your phone on a **stable stand or tripod**. If you don't have one, [ask a helper or use the timer](/guide/take-a-passport-photo-alone).
Use the **highest available camera resolution**.
**Avoid zooming in** or using [portrait mode](/guide/filters-and-portrait-mode).

[Distance](/guide/camera-distance-for-passport-photos): for the rear camera, stand **about 1 to 2 metres** (4 to 6 feet) away. If you use the front camera, hold it **about 40 to 50 cm** (16 to 20 inches) from your face.
**Leave space** above your head and around your shoulders, and **don't crop the photo yourself**. The editor crops it to [your country's size](/guide/passport-photo-sizes-by-country).

items.title: Background
items.alt: A man in front of a plain wall, marked with a tick, next to the same man in front of a bookshelf and patterned wallpaper, marked with a cross

points: Stand in front of a **plain, uncluttered wall**. Most countries ask for a [plain background](/guide/passport-photo-background-rules), often **white, off-white or another light colour**.
Choose a background that **contrasts with your hair and clothing**.
**Stand a little away from the wall** so [your shadow](/guide/avoid-shadows-in-passport-photos) doesn't fall on it.
**Avoid patterned or textured walls**, furniture and other objects in the background.

items.title: Lighting
items.alt: The same face with a shadow on one side and even light on the other

points: Face a window or another [soft light source](/guide/lighting-for-passport-photos), such as **daylight**.
Make sure your face is **evenly lit**, with [no shadows](/guide/avoid-shadows-in-passport-photos) on your face or in the background.
Avoid **harsh sunlight, flash glare and strong shadows**. **Turn the flash off**, and watch out for [red eyes](/guide/red-eye-in-passport-photos).
Do not use **coloured lighting**.

items.title: Face and head position
items.alt: A face looking straight at the camera next to a head turned to the side

groups.label: Head position
points: **Look directly at the camera.**
Keep your [head straight](/guide/head-position-and-size), **not tilted or turned**, and your **shoulders level**.
Make sure your **entire head**, including the top of your hair and your chin, is visible.

groups.label: Facial expression
points: Keep a [neutral expression](/guide/appearance-and-facial-expression) with your **mouth closed**.
Keep **both eyes open** and clearly visible.

A [broad smile with visible teeth](/guide/can-you-smile-in-a-passport-photo) is **not accepted by default**. We allow it only where [your country's page](/guide/photo-requirements-by-country) says it is allowed for your document type.

items.title: Clothing and appearance
items.alt: A face with no glasses next to the same face wearing glasses

points: Wear [simple clothing](/guide/what-to-wear-for-a-passport-photo) that **contrasts with the background**.

**No headwear**, unless it is for [religious or medical reasons](/guide/head-coverings-in-passport-photos). Your **whole face must still be visible**. Some countries ask for a **signed statement**, so check your country's page.
**No decorative hair accessories or fashion hats.** Take off **headphones** too, so nothing covers or frames your face.
**Eyes fully visible:** keep your [hair away from your face](/guide/appearance-and-facial-expression) and eyes.
**Take your glasses off** if you can.

If you need to keep your [glasses](/guide/glasses-in-passport-photos) on, your eyes must be visible **without any glare or reflections**, the **frames must not cover your eyes**, and heavy frames should be avoided. If you can't remove them for medical reasons, your country may ask for a **note from your doctor**.
**No sunglasses or tinted glasses.**
Follow the [selected country's rules](/guide/photo-requirements-by-country) for glasses and head coverings.

items.title: Photo quality
items.alt: A sharp portrait marked with a tick next to the same portrait out of focus, marked with a cross

points: Keep the camera **focused on your face**.
Avoid [blurry or shaky photos](/guide/fix-a-blurry-passport-photo). **Use the timer or a helper.**
Do not use [beauty filters](/guide/filters-and-portrait-mode) or **skin-smoothing effects**.
Upload the **original photo** instead of a screenshot or a [compressed image](/guide/passport-photo-file-size-and-format), such as one sent through a chat app.
Take **at least five photos**, open each one at full size, and pick the **sharpest, evenly lit** one.

items.title: Country specifications
items.alt: Two photos of the same man shown to scale: a 35 x 45 mm rectangle next to a larger 2 x 2 inch square

groups.text: The steps above are the default rules, and they are a good starting point. **Some countries differ from them.** For example, countries can have their own rules on background colour, glasses, head coverings, whether any smile is allowed, [how recent the photo must be](/guide/how-recent-should-a-passport-photo-be), the [photo size](/guide/passport-photo-sizes-by-country), and whether you need a [digital file or a print](/guide/digital-vs-printed-passport-photos). Before you shoot, check your country's [official photo requirements](/guide/photo-requirements-by-country) and follow them. If your country's rules are different from the default rules above, **your country's rules win**.

rows.mistake: Shadows on your face or the wall
rows.fix: Face a window in daylight and stand away from the wall

rows.mistake: Glasses with glare, or a flash that is on
rows.fix: Take your glasses off and turn the flash off
Look straight into the camera with your head level

rows.mistake: A broad smile with visible teeth
rows.fix: Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed, unless your country's page says otherwise

rows.mistake: Filters, portrait mode or beauty mode
rows.fix: Switch them off and use the original photo

faq.title: Photo-at-home questions.
faq.sub: Quick answers about taking your own passport or visa photo.

items.q: Can I take my own passport photo with a phone?
items.a: In many cases, yes, but the rules depend on the country and on how you apply. Check your country's page before you shoot.
You can use the front camera if you hold it about 40 to 50 cm from your face. A photo taken by a helper, or with the timer on a propped-up phone, is usually straighter and steadier.

items.q: Can I keep my glasses on?
items.a: It depends on the country. The safest option is to take them off. Where they are allowed, there must be no glare, no tint, and nothing covering your eyes.
A broad smile with visible teeth is not accepted by default. Some countries allow a closed-mouth smile, and others ask for a neutral expression, so check your country's page.

items.q: Can I use filters or portrait mode?
items.a: No. Don't use filters, beauty mode or editing apps, because the photo should show how you really look.
